# Rollout Plan: Migration of 40,000 Users from Legacy Billing to New Billing System

## Overview

Both billing systems will run in parallel for the duration of the migration (dual-run architecture). Users are migrated in batches; the legacy system continues processing unmigrated users and remains available as a fallback for migrated users until the plan explicitly authorizes its retirement — which is out of scope for this document and must not occur inside the final migration phase.

---

## Phase 1: Pilot (2% of users — ~800 users)

**Entry criterion:** New billing system has passed end-to-end integration tests in staging, including a full billing cycle (invoice generation, payment capture, refund, proration, and tax calculation) with reconciliation against the legacy system showing 100% agreement on a synthetic test dataset of at least 5,000 transactions. Rollback tooling to revert a migrated user back to legacy has been built and tested.

**Population:** Internal employee accounts and opted-in low-risk external users (no active disputes, no complex billing plans such as multi-entity or custom contracts).

**Duration:** 2 weeks minimum.

**Focus:** Validate data migration accuracy, dual-run reconciliation, and basic operational monitoring under real (low-volume) traffic.

---

## Phase 2: Expanded Early Adopters (15% of users — ~6,000 users)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 1 completed its full duration with zero unresolved critical (Sev-1/Sev-2) billing defects, invoice discrepancy rate stayed below the halt threshold (see Metrics), and support ticket volume attributable to billing migration was no higher than the baseline ticket rate for non-migrated users (within a 10% margin). Sign-off obtained from Billing Ops, Finance, and Support leads.

**Population:** A stratified random sample across plan types and geographies, still excluding highest-complexity accounts (enterprise contracts, accounts with active payment disputes, or accounts in active dunning/collections).

**Duration:** 3–4 weeks.

**Focus:** Test migration tooling at higher throughput, validate customer-facing communications and support runbooks, exercise the rollback path on at least one real user cohort.

---

## Phase 3: General Availability Rollout (60% of users — ~24,000 users)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 2 metrics remained within thresholds for its full duration, support escalation rate did not exceed baseline, finance reconciliation between old and new systems balanced to within $0.01 per account across a full billing cycle, and an on-call/incident-response rotation dedicated to migration has been staffed for the duration of this phase.

**Population:** Remaining standard accounts, migrated in weekly waves (e.g., 4–6 waves of ~4,000–6,000 users) to keep each wave individually observable and revertible. Each wave itself requires the prior wave's metrics to be within threshold before proceeding — this is a sub-gate within the phase, not a new named phase.

**Duration:** 6–8 weeks.

**Focus:** Bulk migration at scale while maintaining per-wave rollback capability and continuous reconciliation.

---

## Phase 4: Complex Accounts & Long Tail (23% of users — ~9,200 users)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 3 fully complete with all waves within threshold, and dedicated migration runbooks/tooling built and tested specifically for complex account types (enterprise contracts, multi-entity billing, active disputes/dunning, accounts with custom pricing or grandfathered plans).

**Population:** All remaining users, including the highest-complexity and highest-risk accounts, migrated last specifically because they carry the greatest blast radius if something breaks.

**Duration:** 4–6 weeks, migrated in small, closely monitored batches (e.g., 500–1,000 at a time) given the elevated complexity per account.

**Note:** Legacy system decommissioning is explicitly **not** part of this phase or any phase in this plan. Decommissioning is a separate, subsequent initiative gated on a post-migration stabilization/observation period (recommended minimum 60–90 days with all accounts on the new system and zero open reconciliation discrepancies) and its own sign-off process.

---

## Metrics and Halt Conditions

Rollout halts automatically (no new batches migrated, currently-in-flight batch completes or rolls back) if any of the following occur:

- **Invoice discrepancy rate** between old and new system calculations exceeds **0.1%** of migrated accounts in any 24-hour period.
- **Failed/errored payment capture rate** for migrated users exceeds **0.5%**, or exceeds the pre-migration baseline rate by more than 2x, whichever is lower.
- **Billing-related support ticket volume** from migrated users exceeds **150% of baseline** ticket rate for two consecutive days.
- **Reconciliation job failure**: the automated dual-run reconciliation job fails to complete or shows unreconciled variance greater than **$1,000 in aggregate** across all migrated accounts on any given day.

A halt requires sign-off from Billing Eng and Finance leads before the next batch resumes, and root cause must be documented.

---

## Risks

RISK: Duplicate or double billing occurs during dual-run window if both systems attempt to charge the same user for the same cycle | Implement an idempotency/ownership flag per account marking which system is authoritative for billing that account, enforced at the payment-gateway integration layer, with automated pre-charge checks | Billing Engineering Lead
RISK: Data migration errors (incorrect proration, missing payment methods, wrong tax jurisdiction) corrupt customer billing state | Run automated field-by-field reconciliation between old and new records for every migrated account before and after cutover, with a hard block on migration if reconciliation fails | Data Migration Engineering Lead
RISK: Customers are surprised by a new billing experience (new invoice format, new payment portal) leading to support overload or churn | Send proactive email/in-app notifications at least 7 days before each user's migration, with a clear support escalation path and FAQ | Customer Success Lead
RISK: Rollback of a migrated batch is attempted but legacy system state has drifted out of sync due to the elapsed dual-run period | Freeze and snapshot legacy-system state for each account at the moment of migration and time-box the safe rollback window per batch, with automated staleness alerts beyond that window | Site Reliability Engineering Lead
RISK: Highest-complexity accounts (enterprise, disputed, custom contracts) are migrated too early and cause disproportionate revenue-impacting incidents | Explicitly sequence complex accounts into the final phase only, gated on dedicated tooling and runbooks built and validated against that account class | Billing Product Manager

PHASES: 4
